lines.text: In hiis ergo tribus particulis pars de revolutionibus consummatur.
lines.en: In these three small parts, therefore, the part concerning revolutions is completed.

lines.en: But the part of nativities teaches in the nativities of those whose signi-

lines.en: and the part of fortune, also from the degrees of the ascendant . . . . . . .

lines.en: The part of interrogations again teaches to judge concerning the matter about which the interrogation is made

1 Cf. supra, p. 94, n. 4.
2 Cf. supra, p. 91, n. 3.
3 Omar ben el Ferruchân el Tabarî inter primos astronomos et astrologos suae
aetatis agnoscitur. Mortuus est Bagdadae circa a. 815 p. C. Liber ab Alberto lau-
datus saepius editus est e. g. cum Firmico Materno Basileae 1533; cf. Steinschnei-
der, l. c., p. 373, § 13; Suter, op. cit., p. 7, § 13.
4 Abu'Alî el Chaijât (Jahjâ ben Gâlib), discipulus Masallae (cf. p. 87, n. 3), circa
a. 835 obiit. Ex libris astrologicis quos composuit unus a. 1153 a Iohanne Hispa-
lensi latine versus et a. 1546 et 1549, Norimbergae, editus est (Albohali de iudiciis
nativitatum). Incipit sicut Albertus refert; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 358, § 2;
Suter, op. cit., p. 9, § 17.
5 Est pars secunda libri supra memorati (p. 91, n. 4).
sections.en:
1 Cf. supra, p. 94, n. 4.
2 Cf. supra, p. 91, n. 3.
3 Omar ben el Ferruchân el Tabarî is recognized among the first astronomers and astrologers of his
age. He died at Baghdad around 815 A.D. The book praised by Albertus
has been edited quite often, e.g., with Firmicus Maternus at Basel in 1533; cf. Steinschnei-
der, l. c., p. 373, § 13; Suter, op. cit., p. 7, § 13.
4 Abu'Alî el Chaijât (Jahjâ ben Gâlib), a disciple of Masha'allah (cf. p. 87, n. 3), died around
835. Out of the astrological books which he composed, one was translated into Latin in 1153 by John of Seville
and was edited in 1546 and 1549, at Nuremberg (Albohali de iudiciis
nativitatum). It begins just as Albertus reports; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 358, § 2;
Suter, op. cit., p. 9, § 17.
5 It is the second part of the book mentioned above (p. 91, n. 4).

summary.headline: Nativities and Interrogations
summary.text: John of Seville’s astrological art completes its section on revolutions and begins chapters on nativities and interrogations. The text discusses selecting the hyleg from the luminaries, Part of Fortune, and ascendant degrees, and cites Ptolemy’s Quadripartitus, Aomar of Tiberias, Abuhali, and John of Seville as principal authorities; footnotes identify Omar ben el Ferruchân and Abu’Alî el Chaijât.
